canonical_statement: The study aimed to describe the incidence, management, and outcomes of segmental and subsegmental pulmonary embolism in ICU patients.
The study also explored associations between therapeutic-dose anticoagulation and clinical outcomes in ICU patients with distal pulmonary embolism.
This was a single-center retrospective cohort study conducted in a mixed medical-surgical ICU at Austin Hospital, Melbourne, Australia.
The source population comprised adult ICU patients who underwent at least one CTPA between 1 January 2019 and 30 June 2025.
Eligible patients were critically ill adults aged 18 years or older who underwent CTPA during ICU admission.

population.label: Critically ill adults undergoing CTPA during ICU admission
inclusion_criteria: CTPA performed between ICU admission and ICU discharge

canonical_statement: Patients were included when at least one CTPA during ICU stay showed radiologically confirmed segmental or subsegmental pulmonary embolism.

population.label: ICU patients with radiologically confirmed segmental or subsegmental PE
inclusion_criteria: Segmental or subsegmental PE on CTPA during ICU stay

canonical_statement: Patients with known chronic thromboembolic pulmonary disease or main-trunk or lobar pulmonary emboli were excluded.
Segmental PE was defined as thrombus involving a segmental pulmonary arterial branch, with or without additional subsegmental extension.
Subsegmental PE was defined as thrombus confined to subsegmental branches without involvement of more proximal vessels.
Segmental and subsegmental PE were analyzed together as distal PE, defined as thrombus distal to the lobar pulmonary arteries.
For patients with multiple CTPAs during one ICU admission, the first PE-positive scan was designated the index CTPA and the final radiologist interpretation was used.
Data were extracted from the electronic medical record, radiology information system, pathology databases, and pharmacy dispensing records using a standardized case report form.

Worst physiologic values within six hours of index CTPA and laboratory markers within 24 hours after index CTPA were collected; the closest post-CTPA laboratory value was used when multiple measurements existed.
Formal Wells or Geneva scores were not routinely documented and were not reliably reconstructed; documented clinical features and CTPA indications were extracted instead.
Radiologic variables included PE anatomical level and distribution, right-ventricular dilation or strain, concomitant lower-limb DVT, and ancillary chest CT findings.

Anticoagulation management was classified as prophylaxis before CTPA, therapeutic anticoagulation for another indication before CTPA, any anticoagulation for PE, and therapeutic-dose anticoagulation for PE.
Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation for PE included regimens such as enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily or unfractionated heparin infusion titrated to target aPTT after PE confirmation.

exposures.details: Examples: enoxaparin 1 mg/kg twice daily or UFH infusion titrated to target aPTT

canonical_statement: The primary outcome was the frequency of segmental and subsegmental PE among ICU patients who underwent CTPA during the study period.

concept.text: Frequency of distal PE among ICU CTPA examinations

outcome.definition: Segmental or subsegmental PE among ICU patients undergoing CTPA

canonical_statement: Recurrent VTE was defined as a new objectively confirmed PE or DVT within 90 days from the index scan.

outcome.definition: New objectively confirmed PE or DVT

canonical_statement: Bleeding events were classified using BARC criteria, with major bleeding defined as BARC grade 3 or higher.
Mortality outcomes included in-hospital, 30-day, and 90-day all-cause mortality.
Categorical variables were compared with chi-square or Fisher exact tests and continuous variables with the Wilcoxon rank-sum test; analyses used available cases without imputation.

Prespecified multivariable logistic regression models for therapeutic anticoagulation associations adjusted for age, active cancer, chronic kidney disease, right-ventricular dilation, and concomitant DVT.
For bleeding outcomes, variables with univariable p<0.10 were entered into Firth penalized logistic regression because only 16 bleeding events occurred.
Because only eight recurrence events occurred, no multivariable predictor model for 90-day VTE recurrence was performed beyond the prespecified treatment-association model.

The study used all consecutive eligible patients in the prespecified period and a screening-based descriptive sample-size approach; no separate sample-size calculation was performed for exploratory anticoagulation comparisons.
During the study period, 896 CTPA scans were performed in 804 ICU patients.
Pulmonary embolism was identified on 164 of 896 ICU CTPA examinations (18.3%).

concept.text: Any pulmonary embolism detected on CTPA

canonical_statement: Distal PE was demonstrated on 115 of 896 ICU CTPA examinations (12.8%).
Segmental PE was identified on 68 of 896 ICU CTPA examinations (7.6%).

concept.text: Segmental pulmonary embolism detected on CTPA

canonical_statement: At the patient level, 104 of 804 ICU patients who underwent CTPA had distal PE (12.9%).
After accounting for multiple scans per patient, the final cohort contained 104 unique patients: 61 with segmental PE and 43 with subsegmental PE.
The final cohort had a median age of 61.5 years and 38 of 104 patients (37%) were female.
The cohort included 66 medical, 22 elective surgical, and 16 emergency surgical ICU admissions.
Median APACHE II and APACHE III scores were 17 and 57, respectively.
Among patients with available distribution data, 60% had PE confined to a single lobe, 14% had multiple unilateral involvement, and 26% had bilateral involvement.

canonical_statement: Right-ventricular dilation on CTPA was more common with segmental PE than with subsegmental PE (16% vs 2%; p=0.027).
Concomitant DVT was present in 21 of 104 patients (20%).
Recent surgery was a potential provoking factor in 35 of 104 patients (34%).

canonical_statement: Any bleeding after CTPA occurred in 16 of 104 patients (15%).
Major bleeding (BARC grade 3 or higher) occurred in 12 of 104 patients (12%).
Among 16 patients with documented bleeding, 11 (69%) required red-blood-cell transfusion.
Among 16 patients with documented bleeding, 7 (44%) required an intervention.

canonical_statement: In-hospital mortality was 21 of 104 patients (20%).
Ninety-day mortality was 24 deaths among 98 patients with known 90-day vital status (reported as 24%); six patients had unknown status.
Any bleeding occurred in 16% of segmental PE patients and 14% of SSPE patients (p=0.79).
Major bleeding occurred in 15% of segmental PE patients and 7% of SSPE patients (p=0.35).
Ninety-day recurrent VTE occurred in 10% of segmental PE patients and 5% of SSPE patients (p=0.47).

population.label: Patients in the 90-day recurrence analysis set

canonical_statement: Reported 90-day mortality was 30% in segmental PE and 17% in SSPE (p=0.16).
Median ICU length of stay was 7.2 days (IQR 3.3 to 16.3).
Median hospital length of stay was 21.8 days (IQR 12.3 to 41.5).
Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation was not significantly associated with 90-day mortality (adjusted OR 0.70, 95% CI 0.21 to 2.45).

population.label: Patients in the 90-day mortality treatment-association analysis

canonical_statement: Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation was not significantly associated with any bleeding (adjusted OR 2.34, 95% CI 0.47 to 19.2).
Therapeutic-dose anticoagulation was not significantly associated with 90-day recurrent VTE (adjusted OR 0.69, 95% CI 0.11 to 6.22).

population.label: Patients in the 90-day recurrence analysis set

canonical_statement: In exploratory univariable analysis, right-ventricular dilation was associated with higher 90-day VTE recurrence, but the analysis was based on few recurrence events.
Right-ventricular dilation and anticoagulant class were associated with bleeding in univariable models, but these associations attenuated in penalized regression.
The authors emphasized that bleeding occurred nearly twice as often as VTE recurrence in this ICU distal-PE cohort.
The authors stated that treatment-association estimates should be interpreted as descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than definitive evidence for the optimal anticoagulation strategy.

The authors concluded that the findings highlight uncertainty around routine therapeutic-dose anticoagulation for incidentally identified distal PE in the ICU and support individualized assessment of thrombosis risk, bleeding risk, and illness severity.
The authors called for prospective studies and pragmatic randomized trials to determine which critically ill patients with distal PE benefit from therapeutic versus prophylactic anticoagulation.
The single-center design and modest sample size limited statistical power and generalizability to other practice settings.
Treatment allocation was subject to confounding by indication because treating physicians selected anticoagulation intensity based on clinical factors.
The small numbers of bleeding and recurrent-VTE events reduced statistical precision and produced wide confidence intervals and some non-estimable models.
The study lacked granular data needed to stratify patients with validated bleeding-risk scores.
Formal pre-test probability scores were unavailable, and reliance on documented symptoms and radiology-request indications may incompletely capture clinical reasoning for CTPA.
Clot chronicity could not be determined, and symptom overlap with critical illness may have led to detection of clinically insignificant emboli.
Recurrent-VTE estimates used crude proportions and did not account for death as a competing event, potentially biasing recurrence risk in the setting of high mortality.
Recurrent VTE may have been underdetected because routine follow-up imaging was not performed and recurrence symptoms can overlap with evolving critical illness.
Because of unmeasured confounding and limited precision, the observed lack of association cannot be interpreted as evidence of no treatment effect.
The authors reported receiving no specific funding for the study.
The authors reported no competing interests.
The data availability statement reported that all relevant data are within the manuscript and its Supporting Information files.
